description: Hi! I am a solo participant from India, participating in Mission Solo India. I am working on the challenge - Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts. I love space, technology and problem-solving. I am building a simple dashboard to track astronaut heart rate, oxygen, sleep and give AI health alerts. I am open to collaborate but comfortable working solo too. Let's explore space together!
summary:
Mission Solo India is built for one of the biggest risks in space travel: an astronaut travelling completely alone with no crew to help in an emergency.
We developed a smart, low-cost health monitoring app that connects to a smartwatch and a mobile phone to continuously track vital signs like heart rate, oxygen level, and stress. The app uses a simple Green and Red signal system. Green means the astronaut is safe, Red means immediate danger. This makes it easy to understand even in panic, without any medical knowledge or Mission Control support.
Our solution solves the core challenge of solo missions — isolation and delayed help. By giving early warnings, it helps the astronaut take quick action and stay safe.
It is important because future space missions will be longer, farther, and more isolated. Our solution is affordable, portable, and easy to use, making astronaut safety possible for everyone.
details:
Our project is - Mission Solo India, a Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts.

PROBLEM:

In space, an astronaut is alone, very far from Earth. There is no hospital and no doctor nearby. If the astronaut's health suddenly becomes bad, nobody will know on time. That is why we need a system which can check health continuously.

OUR SOLUTION:

We made a live health monitoring website. It shows the astronaut's health on one screen, like a Mission Control dashboard. Anyone can open it and in one second understand if the astronaut is safe or not.

WHAT IT SHOWS:

On the top, it shows - Mission Solo India and ALL SYSTEMS NORMAL - LIVE.

Below that, there are 4 health cards:

Heart Rate - 77 bpm - Normal. This shows how fast the heart is beating.

Oxygen - 98% - Normal. This shows how much oxygen is in the body.

Temperature - 37°C - Normal. This shows body temperature.

Blood Pressure - 120/80 - Normal. This shows blood pressure.

HOW IT WORKS:

This is a live system. The Heart Rate and Oxygen values change automatically every 2 seconds. For this, we used JavaScript code - setInterval and Math.random. It makes the numbers go up and down like real human body data, for example Heart Rate 70 to 80 bpm and Oxygen 96% to 99%.

Under every value, it shows the word Normal in green colour. Green means everything is safe.

EMERGENCY ALERT SYSTEM:

There is a Test Alert Button at the bottom. When we press it, it shows an alert - ALERT! Doctor ko bulaya ja raha hai!

In this system, the astronaut is above in space, and the doctors are below on Earth. The doctors are watching this system from Mission Control. If there is any problem, the alert goes to the doctors, and the doctors can tell the astronaut which medicine to take and what to do. This project is made for a solo astronaut from India, who is alone in space and far from doctors.

WHY IT IS FOR INDIA:

This project is made for a solo astronaut from India. A solo astronaut has no other team member to help in space, so this software becomes like a doctor friend who is always watching the health.

TOOLS USED:

We used HTML for structure, CSS for design and blue colour cards, and JavaScript for live changing values and alert button. We made the full project on OneCompiler.

FUTURE IDEA:

In future, we can add real sensors, automatic red alert when values become dangerous, and a message system to send health report directly to ISRO / NASA Mission Control.
